# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of `ReelCore.swift`'s
  `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-two op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eight names) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as
  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading GR1) is the plan's Swift side (spec §7.2): `PlanSegment`,
  `PlanRamp`, `PlanTrack`, `PlanInstruction` and `CompositionPlan`; `PlanSpeedRamp.source` is
  its `map` as a `SourceMap`, checked once at decode and not a coding key (SR-20 (c)). `ShapeProps.swift` (a pure
  move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading L3) holds the shape group: `StrokeProps`,
  `GradientStop`, `Gradient` and `ShapeProps`. `GradeProps.swift` holds `ColorAdjust` (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) beside grading's other value types. `ActionSnapshot.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, B87) holds `ActionPatch`, `ActionSnapshot` and `ActionGraphicPatch` — an
  end's `graphic.props` and `kinds`, whose `dictionary` sends `props` only. `MediaSnapshot` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`) carries a copy's or an ffmpeg conversion's `original`, and its `name` is
  the one display-name spelling: the original's name when one is recorded. **Its enums decode LENIENTLY**
  — a misspelt kind becomes the first case, a `T??` field a clear — which is
  why a caller-authored object is never decoded through them (below). The
  one exception is `ClipSource`: an unknown `source.kind` THROWS, and
  `ReelProject.snapshot` then falls back to `.empty`, so the WHOLE project
  draws empty with no error. A new source kind in the core is therefore a
  `ClipSource` case in the same phase (road map 10's G2a added `graphic`): no
  agent handler reads a caller-authored OBJECT at all. A scalar enum
  argument is a different thing and several handlers still parse one by name
  (`enumArg` for `add_zoom_action`'s `fit` or an action's `curve`,
  `set_transition`'s `kind` by hand): the
  core refuses those too, and what this rule forbids is decoding a caller's
  object through a lenient type.
  `MotionProps.dictionary` always writes all three keys, `NSNull` for a nil
  slot, because a core patch of `motion` deep-merges — it is the
  APP's writer saying all three slots, not a replace rule, and it is the only
  edge that writes a whole motion. `MotionEdge` also supplies nonpersisted
  zero-duration activity and inactive display/menu titles (E2-27).
  `TextProps.swift` is the text group and `RecipeReveal` (with format version
  9's `textCase` / `words` / `wordStyle`, the recipe's `word` / `wordPop` and,
  since format version 12, `wordGlide` / `wordFill` / `wordDim`), a pure move
  out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift` because a stored property cannot be added
  from an extension. `RecipeReveal` reads and writes its OWN keys — siblings of
  `hash` and `text` in the `text` source — through `init(siblingsOf:)` and
  `encodeSiblings(to:)`, so a new recipe key costs `FrameRecipe.swift`
  nothing; a key spelled other than the snake-case converter spells it
  decodes silently to that key's default (the amount to 1, the rest to nil).
  `ProjectSnapshot+Graphic.swift` mirrors
  `model_graphic.rs`'s `GraphicProps` as `GraphicSnapshot` (`in` is
  `sourceIn`) and `GraphicPropValue` (string, number, bool; anything else
  `.null`), decoded into `ClipSnapshot.graphic`; `props` keys keep the
  module's own spelling (snake-case conversion does not reach a dictionary's
  keys). `WordProps.swift` mirrors `model_words.rs`
  (`TextCase`, `TextWord`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill`, `WordStyle`)
  — `WordStyle.dictionary` writes ALL eight keys (`active_fill` and `pause_dim` since format version 12; `ActivePill.dictionary` writes `glide`), `NSNull` for a nil slot,
  `MotionProps.dictionary`'s rule, because the core deep-merges
  `word_style` — and holds
  what the renderer and the inspector share: `laidContent` (`case` applied —
  every layout and string index is in ITS UTF-16 space, never `content`'s),
  `tokenCount`, `isUntimedPage`, `TextPatch.contentEdit` and
  `InspectorBinding.contentOps` / `ops(textContent:)` — the Content write,
  decided PER CLIP: `words: []` beside the content in one `set_text` only for
  base clips whose count changed, and never `words` in an action end (W-2,
  W-6). It lives there, not in `InspectorPane.swift`, for the size rule.

**The document.**
- `ProjectDocument.swift` (+`DisplayStem`, +`Recording`, +`SelectedAction`, +`Import`, +`Graphics`, +`GraphicFiles`, +`UndoGroup`, +`CacheSaves`, +`Alerts`)
  — NSDocument, `.framejob` package read/write, and the single mutation
  point (see Undo); `applyEdit`'s `.refused` arm beeps and then posts
  `projectDocumentDidRefuse` with the `ReelRefusal` (spec §11 CI-10), which
  the editor forwards to the inspector's refusal strip. Holds the SIX pieces of view state nothing persists —
  playhead, clip selection, in/out range, `selectedMedia`, `nestPath` and
  `selectedAction` — re-clamped by `clampViewState` in that order with the
  scope FIRST, since the selection clamp measures against whatever
  container the scope left. `selectedAction` (spec §11 CI-1) is nil or one
  action of the SINGLE selected clip; `+SelectedAction` holds its queries,
  its one deliberate writer `selectAction(_:)` (which stores nil for an id
  that is not `singleSelectedClip`'s) and the ENTRY rule
  `syncSelectedAction()`, run from `playhead`'s and `selection`'s `didSet`
  against `lastInsideAction`. The clamp re-reads `lastInsideAction` BEFORE
  its last line writes the playhead, so an edit, undo or redo under a
  stationary playhead never enters a span — keep those two lines above
  that write. `nestPath` is a
  PATH of (nest, clip) steps, not a nest id, because two clips can show one
  nest at two starts; `editedProject` is a STORED, memoised `rc_project_scoped`
  handle, and `project` still means the parent for save, export and
  consolidate. A range is cleared on every scope change: a pair of ticks means
  one thing inside a nest and another to an export. `+UndoGroup`:
  `inUndoGroupIfRegistered` runs a body with an undo group pending, and
  `registerUndo(restoring:actionName:)`'s first statement
  (`openPendingUndoGroup()`) opens it at the body's first registration, at the
  body's level and never while undoing or redoing; a body that registers
  nothing leaves undo and redo untouched (#167); `registerUndo` stays the one
  registrar. `applyEdit(_:_:amending:)` (#272) undoes the step that ended at
  `step` before committing, when `project` is still that handle, so a strip's
  off-knob double-click is one step. `cacheDirectory` calls `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` when it
  creates `cache/` — only if the package's date, read through a fresh `URL`
  before the create, is still `fileModificationDate`, so an outside change made before it is not absorbed — and that method re-reads the date through a fresh
  `URL`, because `fileURL` still holds the date it cached at open (#138).
  `+CacheSaves` is the `save(to:ofType:for:completionHandler:)` override
  every save funnels through, bracketing it with the cache ledger's
  `saveBegan` / `saveEnded` (#115, #169).
  `+Import` is File ▸ Add Media… and every drop into an open project
  (`importMedia`, the probe chain and the one grouped commit), the opening
  read's probe (`probeForOpening`, a cancelled copy as `.userCancelled`), and the Media
  tab's Relink… and the missing-media sheet's body (`relinkMedia(_:)`: each
  file probed through `MediaImporter.probe`, one grouped "Relink Media" edit
  carrying each descriptor as `relink_media`'s `probe`, spec §11 #63, then
  `generateCaches()`; the missing-media sheet's door then alerts each
  unreadable file and each refused sentence (#180) through `present(_:)`).
  `+MissingCopies` re-copies, on open, a WebM/MKV copy that is missing or in
  the Trash from its recorded original (spec §11 #228-O), through
  `MediaImporter.probeBuiltInCopy` (never ffmpeg, never a question); a
  read on main or inside `withoutAsking` (an agent's `open_project`, off
  main since #231) passes no watch.
  `+Alerts` is `present(_:)`: every error the document shows waits in one
  queue (`DocumentAlertQueue`) and shows one alert sheet at a time, each asked
  for a main-queue turn after the last one's `didPresent` or the window's last
  sheet end, and only while no sheet is attached, since AppKit drops an error
  sheet asked for while another is attached (#195, `relink_sheet_probe.py`
  A1–A5); with no window, it is app-modal at once. `+Graphics`
  is the document's side of the package's `graphics/`:
  `startGraphicStore()`, run from `makeWindowControllers()` and seeding an
  untitled document's root from `autosavedContentsFileURL/graphics`, and
  `graphicsWrapper()`, the lazy wrapper the save whitelist carries — for a
  SAVED document it reads `<fileURL>/graphics` itself and never asks the
  store, so a nil store can never drop a saved folder; for an untitled one
  it carries the store's root only when `GraphicStore.holdsContent` (an
  entry, file or directory, that is neither hidden nor the manual) says so
  (spec §11 G-14).
  `startGraphicStore()` also installs the document's compiled set in
  `GraphicRegistry` and observes the store's `.graphicsDidChange`, whose
  handler updates the registry and THEN posts `.projectGraphicsDidChange`
  (object: the document) — never `rescan()` there; `stopGraphicStore()`, from
  `close()`, removes the observer, drops the set, stops the store and removes
  BOTH untitled roots — the graphics root (`removeScratchRoot()`) and
  `temporaryCacheDirectory` (`removeTemporaryCacheDirectory()`); the cache
  root goes at close ONLY, never at the first save, because the timeline and
  any pass in flight still hold its path (G-19 (d)). `startGraphicStore()` also observes the document's own
  `.projectDocumentDidChange` and ends with one `reconcileGraphicNames()`;
  `stopGraphicStore()` removes that observer. `+ConvertedThumbnails`:
  `startCaches()`, from `makeWindowControllers()` in place of
  `generateCaches()`, observes the document's own `.projectDocumentDidChange`
  and starts a cache pass for each media whose converting Camera Log differs
  from the ledger's `lastInput` (spec §11 GR-21); `stopGraphicStore()` removes
  that observation with the rename repair's. `+GraphicFiles` holds the three
  bodies BOTH doors call — `deleteGraphic(named:)` (refused while a clip
  draws the module, naming the clips per container),
  `renameGraphic(named:to:apply:)` (the file, its history, then one
  `set_graphic {name}` per container handed to `apply` as ONE step, moved
  back when `apply` throws or leaves a clip behind, the journal put back as
  it was read before the rename — only when the move back succeeded, so a
  failed one keeps its pair for the repair (G-28 (d)); refused with a nest
  open) and `restoreGraphic(named:revision:)` (which refuses a kept file
  whose bytes are not the revision in its name, G-29 (d)) — each ending its
  file act in one `rescan()`, every throw of its own a `ReelCoreError`; and
  the repair `reconcileGraphicNames()` (spec §11 G-28 (e)): after every
  committed change and once at the store's start, a journalled pair `[a, b]`
  says the app moved the file from `a` to `b`, and when a clip draws `a`,
  with no file and NO kept revision, while `b` has a file and no clip, the
  file is moved back from `b` — one direction only, never from a pair's
  first name to its second (G-28 (e), (f)) — and a file-less name WITH kept
  revisions is left alone even when a crash inside a rename, not a delete,
  left it so (G-28 (f)): it is otherwise a deleted module (G-27 (f)). Never
  call it, or any of the three bodies, from a `.graphicsDidChange` or
  `.projectGraphicsDidChange` observer.
- `MediaImporter.swift` (+`Probe`, +`Speech`, +`Peaks`, +`Color`: the
  Apple Log and Apple Log 2 labels read at probe, spec §11 GR-16, and
  `detectedPQ`, a PQ file's HDR10 peak through `ReelHDR10`, HD-6, and
  `detectedStillPQ`, a PQ still's through `ReelHDR10.stillPeak`, HD-20;
  +`ThumbnailSource`: the converted strip, below; +`Thumbnails`: the
  await-free halves of `thumbnails`, the image branch and the publish) ·
  `MediaPeakBuckets.swift` · `MediaCacheFiles.swift` · `MediaCacheLedger.swift` ·
  `MediaCacheLane.swift` ·
  `FFmpegRewrap.swift` (+`Plan`) · `AppSupport.swift` · `DecoderSupport.swift` ·
  `CodecLibraries.swift` (the SVT-AV1 and libvpx link and its `-RCCodecProbe`;
  export rows arrive with road map codec-export's C1) ·
  `ContainerRewrap.swift` (+`Writer`) · `RewrapProgress.swift` ·
  `RewrapProgressWindowController.swift` — the import funnel and the three per-media caches (`thumbs/`, `peaks/`,
  `speech/`) inside the package. `DecoderSupport.swift` (await-free) is the
  per-process opt-in to macOS's supplemental VP9 and AV1 decoders (`enable()`:
  `main.swift`, `generateCaches`, `CompositionBuilder.firstTrack`, the harness
  and the formats probe), the import's one-frame decode (`decodesFirstFrame`,
  refusing only for `refusingErrorCodes`, -11833 and -11855) and the codec

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

1	# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules
2	
3	Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
4	lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
5	`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
6	§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
7	each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
8	`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
9	line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
10	governs a module now.
11	
12	## Module map
13	
14	- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
15	- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its tracks, clips, sources,
16	  actions, markers and nests, with the serde defaults that say what an absent
17	  key means. The struct field names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here
18	  but `CanvasOutput` (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when
19	  `hlg`, format 23, spec §11 HD-2).
20	- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
21	  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
22	  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
23	- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
24	  (`VideoProps`, `AudioProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`,
25	  `Filter`, `Reflection`, `BlendMode`, `Compressor`, `Duck`) and their
26	  defaults, re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every `crate::model::X` path
27	  holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and `TrackMatte`'s declaration
28	  ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
29	  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
30	  compares against the same integers): append,
31	  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
32	  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
33	- `model_text.rs` · `model_shape.rs` · `model_regions.rs` · `model_motion.rs`
34	  — the text, shape, region and motion vocabularies, each re-exported through
35	  `model_props.rs`. Text and shape are the two sources the model only
36	  DESCRIBES and the platform draws and measures: nothing in either file is
37	  ever a measured size. Regions (`Spotlight`, `ObscureRegion`, `SpotShape`,
38	  `MAX_OBSCURE`) share one coordinate frame — the centre as an offset in
39	  SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect — which
40	  `edit_zoom.rs` writes out as an equation and nothing else restates. The
41	  one load-bearing declaration order in these four is `ObscureKind`'s
42	  (`model_regions.rs`), a shader discriminant like `BlendMode`'s above;
43	  elsewhere only the JSON spelling of every variant is, so a rename needs a migration step. The enums are closed:
44	  there is no neutral kind to fall back to.
45	- `model_words.rs` — the word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road
46	  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
47	  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
48	  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
49	  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11
50	  W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by default: `ActivePill.glide`,
51	  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in
52	  `props_check.rs`); `Word.end` is read by the recipe since then, not only
53	  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
54	  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
55	  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
56	  `token_count`, THE token rule (`split_whitespace` — the core is the one
57	  counter, spec §11 W-2), and `rebase_words`, the one saturating
58	  subtraction `trim_start`, `roll`, `add_transition`'s handle form and
59	  `split`'s second half make (W-3). Word times are clip-time POSITIONS: a
60	  negative start is legal, equal starts are legal, and `snap_animation`
61	  puts them on the grid after `check_text` has named what the caller sent.
62	- `model_graphic.rs` — the graphic vocabulary (format version 10, road
63	  map 10): `GraphicProps` (`name`, `width`, `height`, `in`, `length`,
64	  `props`) and `GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` and the schema limits
65	  `GRAPHIC_MAX_PROPS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_OPTIONS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_STRING` /
66	  `GRAPHIC_TYPES` (`GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` restates the engine's `MAX_SIDE` and the
67	  header's `RC_GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE`, and each other `GRAPHIC_<X>` the engine's
68	  `<X>`; `tests/graphic_ffi.rs`'s
69	  `one_max_side_in_the_engine_the_core_and_the_header` and its four
70	  `one_…_in_the_engine_and_the_core` tests pin them),
71	  re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD `Clip.graphic` stays in
72	  `model.rs`. And the `pub(crate)` checks every writer shares: `check_name`
73	  (G-3's `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, its clause `NAME_RULE` shared with
74	  `validate`), `check_side`, `check_schema` (the engine's sentences, COPIED —
75	  no module of the model may name the crate, G-2; a non-boolean `animate`
76	  on an entry is refused, G-41), `check_props` (by dotted
77	  path against the schema the op carries, shape only without one; a `null`
78	  is a removal and is never checked), `check_typed` (one value against its
79	  entry, answered normalised; `edit_action_graphic.rs` calls it under
80	  `graphic.props.<key>`), `check_count` (on the map about to be
81	  STORED). **A props map is changed only by `insert` and
82	  `shift_remove`**: under `preserve_order`, `Map::remove` is `swap_remove`,
83	  and `Project ==` cannot see the reorder.
84	- `model_look.rs` — the look vocabulary (spec §11 GR-7): `Look {kind, amount}`
85	  (the FIELD `VideoProps.look`, optional, written only when set) and the eight
86	  built-in looks' definitions as data — Color's four, Light's nine and a split
87	  tone each — which the recipe's `look` key carries whole, so retuning a look
88	  is a core change only. `actions.rs` turns a merged look with no valid `kind`
89	  into `null`, so an action's end can never drop the clip's video group.
90	  `kind: "lut"` names an imported LUT's media (`media`); `BUILT_IN` is the
91	  eight. `actions.rs`'s object discriminants (`kind`, `media`) switch at an
92	  action's end instead of interpolating.
93	- `model_grade.rs` — tier 2's grading vocabulary (format 16, spec §11 GR-11): `Wheels {lift,
94	  gamma, gain}`, each a `Wheel {x, y, master}`, the FIELD `VideoProps.wheels` written only when
95	  not neutral and each key only when not 0; `actions::wheels_json` writes all nine for the
96	  evaluator, the patch template and the recipe, as `color_json` does tone's. Format 17 (GR-12)
97	  adds `Curves {master, red, green, blue}`, each an optional list of 2–16 `[x, y]` points
98	  (`CurvePoint`), the FIELD `VideoProps.curves` written only when not the identity
99	  (`curve_is_identity`: every y = x, from x 0 to x 1); format 20 (GR-32) adds `hue_hue` and
100	  `hue_sat` (`[hue, value]` points, 0 ≤ hue < 360) and `CurveDomain` (each channel's identity,
101	  neutral and value range; `named()` and `named_mut()` give each channel's), a hue curve the
102	  identity when every value is its neutral; `actions_curves.rs`'s `curves_json` writes all
103	  six, an absent one as its domain's identity. Format 18 (GR-13) adds `Qualifier {hue,
104	  saturation, luma, invert}` (`HueRange {center, width, softness}` in degrees, `LevelRange
105	  {low, high, softness}` 0–1, a range `None` when off), the FIELD `VideoProps.qualifier`,
106	  written only when not neutral; it acts only on an adjustment clip. Format 21 (GR-35)
107	  adds `Qualifier.blur` (0…1, written only when above 0, after `invert`) and
108	  `QUALIFIER_BLUR_MAX`; `is_neutral` counts it, so a blur alone is kept. Re-exported whole
109	  by `model_props.rs`.
110	- `cube.rs` — the `.cube` reader (spec §11 GR-8): 3D only, size 2–65, the
111	  default domain; anything else refused by line and name. `ffi_cube.rs` — the
112	  four `rc_cube_*` exports. `lut.rs` — a LUT media's rules: placing one is
113	  refused, removing one clears the looks that name it (the clips stay) and
114	  the Camera Log of the media it converts, refusing first without
115	  `with_clips`; paste carries it by path. `Project::check_lut_reference` is
116	  the one check of a LUT named by media id, keyed by its field
117	  (`video.look.media`, `color.lut`).
118	- `model_media_color.rs` — camera log's vocabulary (format version 19,
119	  spec §11 GR-16): `LogCurve`, `CameraGamut` (`LogCurve::gamuts`, its
120	  default first) and `MediaColor` (`log`, `gamut`, `lut`, `detected`, and
121	  since format 22 `pq`, a `PqColor` — import's `file` reading, its
122	  `PeakSource`, the override `peak`, `PEAK_MIN`..`PEAK_MAX` — each written
123	  only when set; format 25 adds `canon_log2`, `canon_log3` and the gamut
124	  `cinema_gamut`, each Canon curve pairing with Cinema Gamut (its default)
125	  or BT.2020, spec §11 HD-17), re-exported by `model.rs` for `Media.color`.
126	  `media_color.rs` — its rules: `set_media_color` (a strict reader,
127	  `detected` and `pq` refused, its `peak` the override, "needs log or lut"
128	  judged on what the caller asked for, spec §11 HD-12),
129	  `check_media_color` (each refusal its own sentence; `add_media` and
130	  `validate` call it too; a `pq`-only colour stands), `without_camera_log`
131	  (what a LUT's removal or a paste leaves: the reading), `media_input` (the
132	  recipe layer's and the plan segment's `input`, with the effective `peak`)
133	  and `media_converted_by`.
134	- `dynamic_range.rs` — an HLG project's deliverables (spec §11 HD-5,
135	  HD-14): `DynamicRange` (`hlg`, `pq`, `sdr`), spelled `dynamic_range` both
136	  as an export override and as a recipe option; `deliverable` answers `None`
137	  for an audio row and for every row of an SDR project, else the picture:
138	  the six HDR rows (`hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `prores_422`, `prores_4444`) carry

142	  codec-export C1): `av1C` built from a full parse of the sequence header OBU,
143	  temporal delimiters stripped in place, and the `av01` brand put into `ftyp`
144	  (no `mp41` to replace is an error, never a file without `av01`); the three
145	  `rc_av1_*` exports. `leb128` is shared with `hdr10.rs`. The export table's
146	  `writer` field (`svt_av1` on `av1` and `av1_webm`; `avf_preset` stays the ImageIO
147	  switch) and the `encoder_speed` override (`faster` | `balanced` | `smaller`,

150	- `export_encoder.rs` — the bundled encoders' route and speeds (spec §11
151	  CX-12, CX-16): `Writer` (`svt_av1`, `libvpx`; none is AVFoundation; `takes_speed`
152	  false for libvpx's one speed) and `EncoderSpeed`, moved whole out of
153	  `export_table.rs` (codec-export C3's toll, a pure move) and re-exported there.
154	- `export_preset.rs` — `Preset`, its `impl` and `fps_json`, moved whole out of
155	  `export_table.rs` (codec-export C5's toll T1, a pure move) and re-exported there.
156	- `webm_ebml.rs` · `webm_layout.rs` · `webm_writer.rs` · `ffi_webm.rs` — the

159	  and AlphaMode 1, `add_video_with_alpha`), the write side beside
160	  the importer's reader: `webm_ebml.rs` the element IDs, vints and builders
161	  (EBML header, Info, the TrackEntries with Colour and OpusHead, Chapters,
162	  SeekHead) with `webm_ebml_block.rs` the Cues and block builders and the alpha BlockGroup
163	  (BlockAdditions, BlockAddID 1, a ReferenceBlock on non-key blocks; C5's toll T2);
164	  `webm_layout.rs` `rc_webm_open`'s JSON as `WebmLayout`, each
165	  value checked in a sentence naming it; `webm_writer.rs` `WebmWriter`, the

170	- `graphic_package.rs` · `ffi_graphic_package.rs` — the `.fjgraphic` package
171	  (spec §11 G-46): the package request's checks, the in-package name
172	  legaliser (legal names claimed first, G-23 (c)'s suffixes on a clash),

181	- `hdr10.rs` · `ffi_hdr10.rs` — an HDR10 file's peak (spec §11 HD-6,

193	  and clamp as `hdr10.rs`. Pure, every index checked against the buffer.
194	- `model_matte.rs` — the matte vocabulary (format version 14, spec §11 MT-1):
195	  `TrackMatte` (`none`, `alpha`, `alpha_inverted`, `luma`, `luma_inverted`)
196	  and `is_none`, re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD
197	  `Track.matte` stays in `model.rs`, skipped when `none` (an ordinary track
198	  writes no key), as `ColorAdjust`'s nine tone keys are when 0.
199	- `model_color.rs` — `normalise_color`, G-12's colour grammar (hex,
200	  `rgb()`/`rgba()`, `hsl()`/`hsla()` and the CSS named colours, from
201	  svgtypes' table) to lowercase `#rrggbb[aa]`; out of range is refused,
202	  never clamped. The stdlib's `__parseColour` implements the same grammar,
203	  and both suites read `graphic/tests/colours.json`. `rc_normalise_color`
204	  (`ffi.rs`) exports it for the Inspector's colour defaults (spec §11 G-25
205	  (c)), and `model_graphic.rs`'s `check_schema` refuses a `color` default
206	  it refuses (G-25 (a)). `color_channels` and `color_hex` (which
207	  `normalise_color` writes through) and `oklab_mix` are
208	  `actions_graphic.rs`'s blend's: `oklab_mix` is the stdlib's
209	  `interpolateColors` ported operation for operation (spec §11 G-40), now
210	  bytes/255 through `oklab_mix_unit` and ×255 rounded out; `oklab_mix_unit`
211	  and `oklab_mix_rgb` (0–1 floats, clamped, never rounded) are
212	  `actions_color.rs`'s (G-43). Three suites read `graphic/tests/oklab.json`:
213	  the stdlib's, `graphic_actions.rs` and `action_colours.rs`.
214	- `model_query.rs` — reading a project: `Project::new`, id allocation, the
215	  `clip`/`track`/`media`/`marker`/`nest` lookups, `clips_on`, `duration`,
216	  `validate` with its nesting walk, and `source_size`; and the shared
217	  spellings of a fresh thing: `Track::ordinary` (every flag off),
218	  `Source::media` (the media a source reads, exhaustive over the kinds),
219	  `next_track_name` ("Track N" by the count), `numbered_track` (allocated
220	  and named, not inserted) and `remint` (a copied clip's fresh ids: the
221	  clip's, then each action's). The three source-window measurements moved
222	  out to `source_window.rs`.
223	- `frame_grid.rs` — clip-time normalization shared by canvas rate changes,
224	  both full-paste paths and unnest. It snaps placement start, delegates the
225	  source-bounded duration to `source_window.rs`, clamps action spans, snaps
226	  present base motion/text timing through the patch snappers, and snaps a
227	  graphic's `in` and `length` through `recipe_graphic.rs`'s
228	  `graphic_resnapped` (spec §11 G-18). It does not change source positions,
229	  action-end payloads or audio envelopes. On a ramped clip (SR-19 (g))
230	  `resnap_actions` snaps the speed actions without clamping them into the
231	  clip (clamping would change what it reads), and `resnap_clip_times` holds
232	  the duration a second time over the snapped map.
233	- `source_window.rs` — THE source window: how much material a clip shows,
234	  how much lies either side of it, and the one way a source in point moves.
235	  `content_length_in_source` reads `speed_map.rs`'s map for a ramped clip
236	  (SR-10), so the one function still says how much source any clip reads.
237	  On a ramped clip (SR-18) the tail readers go through `time_for_source`,
238	  `in` moves by `source_read_by` / `source_advanced_through` (trims, roll,
239	  split, freeze), `front_edge_held` bisects the front edge to a frame that
240	  fits, and `window_of` / `overrun` (moved here from `edit_action_speed.rs`)
241	  are the fit test.
242	  **Every name here carries its UNIT**, because the readers divide by a
243	  clip's speed where the movers multiply by it: `content_length_in_source`,
244	  `last_in_point` and `last_still_time` answer in SOURCE ticks;
245	  `source_head_on_timeline`, `source_length_on_timeline` and
246	  `longest_duration_on_grid` — the bound, snapped DOWN (spec §11, #22) — in
247	  TIMELINE ticks. **Every site that WRITES a media clip's window reads the
248	  bound here, and which function it reads says what it writes** (spec §11,
249	  D4-2 to D4-5): `longest_duration_on_grid_of` is the bound from the pieces,
250	  with the clip's `start` among them, because a DURATION is measured from 0
251	  and an END from the clip's own start and the two are not the same number;
252	  `latest_end_on_grid` and `earliest_start_on_grid` are the timeline
253	  POSITIONS `trim_end` / `roll` and `trim_start` / `roll` /
254	  `head_handle_frames` clamp to (positions, so not a `SourceBound`);
255	  `duration_resnapped` is what every RE-SNAP of a media duration writes
256	  (`resnap`, `paste` twice, `unnest`, `relink_media`'s hold to a shorter file)
257	  and `duration_at_speed` what
258	  `set_speed` writes. No local clamp anywhere else. A measurement is a
259	  `SourceBound` and not an `Option`,
260	  because `None` meant "unbounded, apply no clamp" to a trim and "no handle

594	  clip lacks (`schema_default`; an asset's is its string default or `""`); `write_graphic_end` stores `props` and `kinds` by

596	- `edit_paste_attributes.rs` — `paste_attributes`, cut out of `edit_paste.rs`
597	  under the size rule as a pure move ahead of spec §11 G-32: the payload's
598	  EARLIEST clip's property groups (then the front-most, then the lower id —
599	  never the array's first) copied onto each target, replaced whole and never
600	  merged. `PasteGroup` is the five names it takes — the four patch groups and
601	  `graphic`, which is never in the default set: a graphic's `props` copied
602	  whole onto clips drawn by the SAME module, the target keeping its name,
603	  size, `in` and `length`, written with `insert` and `shift_remove`
604	  (`model_graphic.rs`'s rule). A target key the payload lacks that an
605	  action on the target names (`names_prop`) is kept (G-34 (d), amending
606	  G-32 (e)). `skip_missing` drops a named group the payload
607	  clip lacks and skips a target that cannot take one. **The copied props are

609	  takes never reads the map. `patch::Group` gains no variant for it.

613	  required (a list is not read member by member), an unknown or missing
614	  member named, a wrong-typed one named by its path. **Its module doc

618	- `edit_adjustment.rs` — `Source::Adjustment`'s rules (spec §11 GR-6):

620	  transition (from `add_transition`, `set_transition`, `set_transition_style`
621	  and the overlap rule), a nest, and the blur, sharpen and pixelate filters
622	  and any blend mode. The recipe draws it as `{"kind":"adjustment"}` (plus its `qualifier` when
623	  it has one and `selection: true` when `RecipeOptions.selection` names it, GR-13); and on a
624	  matte track it is dropped before the frame's mattes (inert).
625	- `edit_background.rs` — `add_background` and `add_blurred_background`: one
626	  clip on a NEW back-most track, OPS rather than app-side composites because
627	  the composite carries constraints no half states. A blurred copy drops
628	  `enabled.audio`, `audio.duck`, the transition, the actions and the label
629	  (each a wrong picture or a wrong sound if carried) and refuses a nest.
630	  Default plate colour is white: the canvas is already black.
631	- `actions.rs` — action evaluation and interpolation, and `clip_state`
632	  (with a top-level `speed`, `speed_map.rs`'s rate in force, the inspector's
633	  Rate inside an action, SR-21);
634	  `video_json` / `color_json` write all thirteen colour keys, the tone keys at
635	  0 included, for the five callers that must see them (the base state,
636	  `clip_state`, `patch.rs`'s template, `recipe_layer.rs`, `edit_split.rs`);
637	  its last line of defence is `actions_clamp.rs`'s, and a graphic's props
638	  are `actions_graphic.rs`'s (spec §11 G-34), carried in `Evaluated.graphic`
639	  and `clip_state`'s `graphic`. **The LIST rule is stated here once as the
640	  crate's**: an end patch interpolates a list per index when the lengths
641	  match and each pair of entries agrees on its discrete fields (`kind`,
642	  `shape`), and switches at the end otherwise; `video.filters` and `video.obscure` are both governed by it and carry no code of their own.
643	- `actions_clamp.rs` — `clamp_video`, `clamp_audio` and `clamp_text`, the
644	  evaluator's last line of defence (`set_action_end` checks a `video`,
645	  `audio` or `text` end patch's keys and kinds but deliberately not its
646	  VALUES, and never looks at the clip for them; this bounds every value
647	  such a patch can carry and forces `normal` on a nest clip), with
648	  `bounded` / `finite_or`; the first two a pure move out of `actions.rs`
649	  (issue batch B87, toll A), `clamp_text` added by #353.
650	- `actions_curves.rs` — `curves_json` (all six curves, an absent one
651	  as its domain's identity, for `video_json`'s callers),
652	  `align_identity_curves` (spec §11 GR-12, GR-32: an identity curve
653	  meeting a curve of another count in an action takes that curve's x's,
654	  its ends at 0 and 1 on a tone curve and every value the neutral on a
655	  hue curve, so a grade animates from neutral), and `CurveBlend`,
656	  `curve_blends` and `blended_curves_json` (spec §11 GR-34: two
657	  non-identity curves of different counts in an action blend their
658	  values — the evaluator names each such channel with its clamped end
659	  curve and the eased t in `Evaluated.curve_blends`, and only the recipe

661	- `actions_qualifier.rs` — `qualifier_json` (spec §11 GR-35): a qualifier
662	  with its `blur` present even at 0, which `actions.rs`'s `video_json` writes
663	  for a non-neutral one so the blur animates from 0; and `align_hue_center`
664	  (spec §11 GR-13): before
665	  the lerp, an action's target hue centre moves by ±360 when the two
666	  centres are more than 180° apart, so the centre animates the short
667	  way round (350 → 10 through 0); `clamp_qualifier` brings it back
668	  into [0, 360).
669	- `actions_color.rs` — `blend_colors` (spec §11 G-43): after the spanning
670	  action's `lerp`, each of the model's colours — `COLOR_POINTERS`' eight
671	  `[r, g, b, a]` in `video` and `text` and `CHROMA_KEY_POINTER`'s `[r, g,
672	  b]`, by path, never by shape — is overwritten by the OKLab blend of the
673	  action's two ends (`oklab_mix_unit` / `oklab_mix_rgb`), only strictly
674	  inside the action and only where the ends differ, so an untouched colour
675	  stays exact; an end of the wrong arity keeps §5.4's hold-then-switch.
676	- `actions_graphic.rs` — a graphic clip's props at a clip time (format
677	  version 13, spec §11 G-34): finished actions' `end.graphic.props` laid
678	  over the clip's map by `insert`, the spanning one interpolated — a number
679	  in floating point, never rounded; a `color` (by `end.graphic.kinds`,
680	  never by shape) in OKLab with straight alpha through `model_color.rs`'s
681	  `oklab_mix` (G-40); anything else, a malformed end, or a prop
682	  with no start, held and switched at the end. Total. `names_prop` is
683	  `set_graphic`'s and `paste_attributes`' question.
684	- `transition.rs` — overlap detection, THE overlap rule (spec §11), eased
685	  progress at *t*. An overlap with no kind still dissolves
686	  (`unwrap_or_default`), and `add_clip` onto an overlap mints a
687	  `cross_dissolve`, so a no-transition baseline is built by moving clips
688	  apart, not by clearing the kind.
689	- `transition_search.rs` — the bounded fitting arithmetic for both hard-cut
690	  transition forms: the old handle decrement path by total, and exact
691	  forbidden shift intervals across fixed/moved clips for ripple, counted in
692	  whole grid frames back from the cut (`time::frames_within`). It does
693	  not enumerate timeline frames; final placements still pass
694	  `check_overlap_rule`.
695	- `evaluate.rs` — the A/B assignment, `assign()`, that the plan and the
696	  recipe share, and `drawing_instances`, which both the instruction tiling
697	  and the layer list are built from. `assign` leaves a clip's audio out above
698	  `AUDIO_SPEED_MAX`, and `place` gives every plan audio track ONE `pitch`
699	  (#190, #211), a `Pitch` (off, spectral, time_domain): keep pitch within
700	  ×0.999–×1.001 (but not ×1) plays `off`, varispeed, whose pitch change is
701	  under 1.74 cents (SY-39), and elsewhere within ×0.98–×1.02 `time_domain`
702	  (SY-26; SY-40 for real speed changes). `Segment`, `CompTrack` and
703	  `Assignment`'s tracks are `pub(crate)` for `plan.rs` alone. A ramped
704	  clip (speed ramps SR-10) is placed as ONE unit, its frame-per-segment
705	  video and its one ramp audio segment (`ramp`, the source map) on the
706	  same tracks; its ×12 test reads `speed_map.rs`'s `peak_rate` (the greatest
707	  rate named, not reached, SR-19 (d)) of the instance's own, unlifted clip,
708	  the same stored numbers Swift's `SpeedAudioDrop.peakSpeed` reads.
709	- `plan.rs` — `composition_plan()` (spec §7.2): the plan's JSON from
710	  `assign()`, the instruction tiling, and the decoder-budget warning
711	  (`MAX_CONCURRENT_VIDEO_TRACKS`). Deterministic to the byte. A pure move
712	  out of `evaluate.rs` (grading GR1).
713	- `recipe.rs` · `recipe_layer.rs` · `recipe_options.rs` · `recipe_selection.rs` ·
714	  `recipe_text.rs` — `frame_recipe(t)`: the layer list at one instant. `RecipeLayer`
715	  (`recipe_layer.rs`, re-exported by
716	  `recipe.rs`) is the twenty-six keys of a layer written in ONE place
717	  (`RecipeLayer.init(from:)` on the Swift side defaults a missing key
718	  silently, so a copied skeleton drifts with no diagnostic). `RecipeOptions`
719	  (`recipe_options.rs`, a pure move out of `recipe.rs` in grading-2 G2-0, re-exported by it) is
720	  what a caller wanted besides `t` — the burn-in timecode, `ungraded` (spec §11 GR-4: every
721	  layer's `color` written neutral), and `selection` and `behind` (GR-13: `recipe_selection.rs`
722	  marks, or drops, the named adjustment clip's layer and drops every canvas layer in front of
723	  it) — and is a recipe option, never an export override, because the override table drops an
724	  unknown key in silence. A layer whose `transition` or `dissolve` is non-null is
725	  emitted `blend: "normal"` whatever the clip says: one of the core's TWO
726	  deliberate overrides of model values (the other: a matte layer's `blend`,
727	  `shadow` and `reflection`, MT-4), because the dissolve's weight correction
728	  is the inverse of a fixed-function destination factor, and a routed half
729	  (`dissolve`) is drawn alone and mixed source-over (spec §11 MT-8). The
730	  inspector therefore
731	  shows the model's value while the frame draws `normal` during an overlap.
732	  `recipe_text.rs` computes what a text layer SHOWS — `Reveal::of` turns
733	  `text.animation` into `reveal`, `reveal_phase` (the ORDER the renderer draws
734	  in, not a label on the amount) and `reveal_kind`, folded into the content
735	  hash so an animating layer is never served a stale texture — and
736	  `burn_in_layer`. `serde_json`'s `Map` keeps INSERTION order in this
737	  build (`graphic` enables `preserve_order` and cargo unifies it), so
738	  `content_hash` sorts every object's keys before it hashes — the order
739	  every texture key was taken in — and nothing may lean on the wire order
740	  of a map.
741	  A graphic layer's source is one arm calling `recipe_graphic.rs`'s

# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its tracks, clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests, with the serde defaults that say what an absent
  key means. The struct field names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here
  but `CanvasOutput` (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when
  `hlg`, format 23, spec §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `AudioProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`,
  `Filter`, `Reflection`, `BlendMode`, `Compressor`, `Duck`) and their
  defaults, re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every `crate::model::X` path
  holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and `TrackMatte`'s declaration
  ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_text.rs` · `model_shape.rs` · `model_regions.rs` · `model_motion.rs`
  — the text, shape, region and motion vocabularies, each re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`. Text and shape are the two sources the model only
  DESCRIBES and the platform draws and measures: nothing in either file is
  ever a measured size. Regions (`Spotlight`, `ObscureRegion`, `SpotShape`,
  `MAX_OBSCURE`) share one coordinate frame — the centre as an offset in
  SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect — which
  `edit_zoom.rs` writes out as an equation and nothing else restates. The
  one load-bearing declaration order in these four is `ObscureKind`'s
  (`model_regions.rs`), a shader discriminant like `BlendMode`'s above;
  elsewhere only the JSON spelling of every variant is, so a rename needs a migration step. The enums are closed:
  there is no neutral kind to fall back to.
- `model_words.rs` — the word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road
  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11
  W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by default: `ActivePill.glide`,
  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in
  `props_check.rs`); `Word.end` is read by the recipe since then, not only
  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
  `token_count`, THE token rule (`split_whitespace` — the core is the one
  counter, spec §11 W-2), and `rebase_words`, the one saturating
  subtraction `trim_start`, `roll`, `add_transition`'s handle form and
  `split`'s second half make (W-3). Word times are clip-time POSITIONS: a
  negative start is legal, equal starts are legal, and `snap_animation`
  puts them on the grid after `check_text` has named what the caller sent.
- `model_graphic.rs` — the graphic vocabulary (format version 10, road
  map 10): `GraphicProps` (`name`, `width`, `height`, `in`, `length`,
  `props`) and `GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` and the schema limits
  `GRAPHIC_MAX_PROPS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_OPTIONS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_STRING` /
  `GRAPHIC_TYPES` (`GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` restates the engine's `MAX_SIDE` and the
  header's `RC_GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE`, and each other `GRAPHIC_<X>` the engine's
  `<X>`; `tests/graphic_ffi.rs`'s
  `one_max_side_in_the_engine_the_core_and_the_header` and its four
  `one_…_in_the_engine_and_the_core` tests pin them),
  re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD `Clip.graphic` stays in
  `model.rs`. And the `pub(crate)` checks every writer shares: `check_name`
  (G-3's `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, its clause `NAME_RULE` shared with
  `validate`), `check_side`, `check_schema` (the engine's sentences, COPIED —
  no module of the model may name the crate, G-2; a non-boolean `animate`
  on an entry is refused, G-41), `check_props` (by dotted
  path against the schema the op carries, shape only without one; a `null`
  is a removal and is never checked), `check_typed` (one value against its
  entry, answered normalised; `edit_action_graphic.rs` calls it under
  `graphic.props.<key>`), `check_count` (on the map about to be
  STORED). **A props map is changed only by `insert` and
  `shift_remove`**: under `preserve_order`, `Map::remove` is `swap_remove`,
  and `Project ==` cannot see the reorder.
- `model_look.rs` — the look vocabulary (spec §11 GR-7): `Look {kind, amount}`
  (the FIELD `VideoProps.look`, optional, written only when set) and the eight
  built-in looks' definitions as data — Color's four, Light's nine and a split
  tone each — which the recipe's `look` key carries whole, so retuning a look
  is a core change only. `actions.rs` turns a merged look with no valid `kind`
  into `null`, so an action's end can never drop the clip's video group.
  `kind: "lut"` names an imported LUT's media (`media`); `BUILT_IN` is the
  eight. `actions.rs`'s object discriminants (`kind`, `media`) switch at an
  action's end instead of interpolating.
- `model_grade.rs` — tier 2's grading vocabulary (format 16, spec §11 GR-11): `Wheels {lift,
  gamma, gain}`, each a `Wheel {x, y, master}`, the FIELD `VideoProps.wheels` written only when
  not neutral and each key only when not 0; `actions::wheels_json` writes all nine for the
  evaluator, the patch template and the recipe, as `color_json` does tone's. Format 17 (GR-12)
  adds `Curves {master, red, green, blue}`, each an optional list of 2–16 `[x, y]` points
  (`CurvePoint`), the FIELD `VideoProps.curves` written only when not the identity
  (`curve_is_identity`: every y = x, from x 0 to x 1); format 20 (GR-32) adds `hue_hue` and
  `hue_sat` (`[hue, value]` points, 0 ≤ hue < 360) and `CurveDomain` (each channel's identity,
  neutral and value range; `named()` and `named_mut()` give each channel's), a hue curve the
  identity when every value is its neutral; `actions_curves.rs`'s `curves_json` writes all
  six, an absent one as its domain's identity. Format 18 (GR-13) adds `Qualifier {hue,
  saturation, luma, invert}` (`HueRange {center, width, softness}` in degrees, `LevelRange
  {low, high, softness}` 0–1, a range `None` when off), the FIELD `VideoProps.qualifier`,
  written only when not neutral; it acts only on an adjustment clip. Format 21 (GR-35)
  adds `Qualifier.blur` (0…1, written only when above 0, after `invert`) and
  `QUALIFIER_BLUR_MAX`; `is_neutral` counts it, so a blur alone is kept. Re-exported whole
  by `model_props.rs`.
- `cube.rs` — the `.cube` reader (spec §11 GR-8): 3D only, size 2–65, the
  default domain; anything else refused by line and name. `ffi_cube.rs` — the
  four `rc_cube_*` exports. `lut.rs` — a LUT media's rules: placing one is
  refused, removing one clears the looks that name it (the clips stay) and
  the Camera Log of the media it converts, refusing first without
  `with_clips`; paste carries it by path. `Project::check_lut_reference` is
  the one check of a LUT named by media id, keyed by its field
  (`video.look.media`, `color.lut`).
- `model_media_color.rs` — camera log's vocabulary (format version 19,
  spec §11 GR-16): `LogCurve`, `CameraGamut` (`LogCurve::gamuts`, its
  default first) and `MediaColor` (`log`, `gamut`, `lut`, `detected`, and
  since format 22 `pq`, a `PqColor` — import's `file` reading, its
  `PeakSource`, the override `peak`, `PEAK_MIN`..`PEAK_MAX` — each written
  only when set; format 25 adds `canon_log2`, `canon_log3` and the gamut
  `cinema_gamut`, each Canon curve pairing with Cinema Gamut (its default)
  or BT.2020, spec §11 HD-17), re-exported by `model.rs` for `Media.color`.
  `media_color.rs` — its rules: `set_media_color` (a strict reader,
  `detected` and `pq` refused, its `peak` the override, "needs log or lut"
  judged on what the caller asked for, spec §11 HD-12),
  `check_media_color` (each refusal its own sentence; `add_media` and
  `validate` call it too; a `pq`-only colour stands), `without_camera_log`
  (what a LUT's removal or a paste leaves: the reading), `media_input` (the
  recipe layer's and the plan segment's `input`, with the effective `peak`)
  and `media_converted_by`.
- `dynamic_range.rs` — an HLG project's deliverables (spec §11 HD-5,
  HD-14): `DynamicRange` (`hlg`, `pq`, `sdr`), spelled `dynamic_range` both
  as an export override and as a recipe option; `deliverable` answers `None`
  for an audio row and for every row of an SDR project, else the picture:
  the six HDR rows (`hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `prores_422`, `prores_4444`) carry
  `hlg` (the default), `pq` or `sdr`, every other video row writes the SDR
  version, and `hlg`/`pq` are refused in an SDR project and on any other row, each in its own sentence.
- `av1_mp4.rs` · `ffi_av1.rs` — AV1 in MP4 (spec §11 CX-12, road map
  codec-export C1): `av1C` built from a full parse of the sequence header OBU,
  temporal delimiters stripped in place, and the `av01` brand put into `ftyp`
  (no `mp41` to replace is an error, never a file without `av01`); the three
  `rc_av1_*` exports. `leb128` is shared with `hdr10.rs`. The export table's
  `writer` field (`svt_av1` on `av1` and `av1_webm`; `avf_preset` stays the ImageIO
  switch) and the `encoder_speed` override (`faster` | `balanced` | `smaller`,
  refused on any other row) are `export_table.rs`' and `export_overrides.rs`';
  `Container` is `export_container.rs`'.
- `export_encoder.rs` — the bundled encoders' route and speeds (spec §11
  CX-12, CX-16): `Writer` (`svt_av1`, `libvpx`; none is AVFoundation; `takes_speed`
  false for libvpx's one speed) and `EncoderSpeed`, moved whole out of
  `export_table.rs` (codec-export C3's toll, a pure move) and re-exported there.
- `export_preset.rs` — `Preset`, its `impl` and `fps_json`, moved whole out of
  `export_table.rs` (codec-export C5's toll T1, a pure move) and re-exported there.
- `webm_ebml.rs` · `webm_layout.rs` · `webm_writer.rs` · `ffi_webm.rs` — the
  WebM an `av1_webm` or `vp9_webm` export writes (spec §11 CX-6, CX-15, CX-16: `V_VP9` with
  no CodecPrivate, BitsPerChannel 8 or 10; CX-17: `alpha_mode` on `V_VP9`, MaxBlockAdditionID
  and AlphaMode 1, `add_video_with_alpha`), the write side beside
  the importer's reader: `webm_ebml.rs` the element IDs, vints and builders
  (EBML header, Info, the TrackEntries with Colour and OpusHead, Chapters,
  SeekHead) with `webm_ebml_block.rs` the Cues and block builders and the alpha BlockGroup
  (BlockAdditions, BlockAddID 1, a ReferenceBlock on non-key blocks; C5's toll T2);
  `webm_layout.rs` `rc_webm_open`'s JSON as `WebmLayout`, each
  value checked in a sentence naming it; `webm_writer.rs` `WebmWriter`, the
  interleave (earliest head, video first on a tie), Clusters at each key and
  before 32,767 ms, Cues, the SeekHead and the Segment size patched at
  `finish`; `ffi_webm.rs` the six `rc_webm_*` exports over a
  `Mutex<WebmWriter>`. It writes the bytes it is handed and never decodes.
- `graphic_package.rs` · `ffi_graphic_package.rs` — the `.fjgraphic` package
  (spec §11 G-46): the package request's checks, the in-package name
  legaliser (legal names claimed first, G-23 (c)'s suffixes on a clash),
  `manifest.json`, the stored zip and its CRC-32, and the write (`.partial`
  renamed into place); names no `graphic` item. `graphic_package_read.rs`
  is the reader (G-47): stored entries only, `manifest.json` first,
  `"fjgraphic": 1` (a newer version refused by number), each file's size and
  SHA-256 against the manifest, no path out of `fonts/`/`assets/`; it
  answers the checked manifest and each file's offset. `ffi_graphic_package.rs`
  is `rc_graphic_package_write`, answering the manifest it wrote, and
  `rc_graphic_package_read`.

  both full-paste paths and unnest. It snaps placement start, delegates the
  source-bounded duration to `source_window.rs`, clamps action spans, snaps

  graphic's `in` and `length` through `recipe_graphic.rs`'s
  `graphic_resnapped` (spec §11 G-18). It does not change source positions,
  action-end payloads or audio envelopes. On a ramped clip (SR-19 (g))

  clip (clamping would change what it reads), and `resnap_clip_times` holds

- `source_window.rs` — THE source window: how much material a clip shows,
  how much lies either side of it, and the one way a source in point moves.
  `content_length_in_source` reads `speed_map.rs`'s map for a ramped clip
  (SR-10), so the one function still says how much source any clip reads.
  On a ramped clip (SR-18) the tail readers go through `time_for_source`,
  `in` moves by `source_read_by` / `source_advanced_through` (trims, roll,
  split, freeze), `front_edge_held` bisects the front edge to a frame that
  fits, and `window_of` / `overrun` (moved here from `edit_action_speed.rs`)
  are the fit test.

  clip's speed where the movers multiply by it: `content_length_in_source`,
  `last_in_point` and `last_still_time` answer in SOURCE ticks;
  `source_head_on_timeline`, `source_length_on_timeline` and
  `longest_duration_on_grid` — the bound, snapped DOWN (spec §11, #22) — in

  bound here, and which function it reads says what it writes** (spec §11,
  D4-2 to D4-5): `longest_duration_on_grid_of` is the bound from the pieces,
  with the clip's `start` among them, because a DURATION is measured from 0
  and an END from the clip's own start and the two are not the same number;
  `latest_end_on_grid` and `earliest_start_on_grid` are the timeline
  POSITIONS `trim_end` / `roll` and `trim_start` / `roll` /
  `head_handle_frames` clamp to (positions, so not a `SourceBound`);
  `duration_resnapped` is what every RE-SNAP of a media duration writes
  (`resnap`, `paste` twice, `unnest`, `relink_media`'s hold to a shorter file)
  and `duration_at_speed` what

  `SourceBound` and not an `Option`,
  because `None` meant "unbounded, apply no clamp" to a trim and "no handle
  at all" to a transition: the three arms are `Unbounded` (a source with no
  window), `Unmeasured` (a media window that exists and cannot be measured)
  and `Timeline`, and a caller picks what `Unmeasured` means to it BY NAME,
  `or_unbounded` or `or_empty`. `in_advanced` / `source_advanced` is the one
  `round(Δ × speed)` mover the six placement sites used to write out. Cut
  out of `model_query.rs` by road map 7 §10's phase A.

  public tick/index result. `frames_in` (whole grid frames in a length),
  `frames_back` (the grid position k frames before the frame nearest a
  position) and `frames_within` (the most whole frames back from a position
  that stay within a span), `frames_between` (the whole grid frames between
  two positions) and `one_frame` (the grid's own first frame, which
  `Project::frame` is at every rate, 1/30 s only at a degenerate rate; spec
  §11 #174) count on the canvas's own grid at a rate the
  timescale does not divide (spec §11 #42).
- `time_bounds.rs` — the single structural-time admission checker and
  `MAX_STORED_TICKS`: ±9,000,000,000,000,000 for stored media, markers,
  clips, source positions and actions, including clip/action endpoints in
  i128. `Project::validate` and `format::write` both call it; vocabulary
  property timings and finite positive speeds are outside this envelope.
- `outcome.rs` — `Outcome`, the THREE arms every edit answers with
  (spec §5.5): applied with the new project, an identity, or refused with
  the rule's own sentence. An enum and its doc, nothing else. It is an enum
  rather than a side channel so that a site which has not decided which
  answer it gives does not compile; the fourth possibility, a request that
  could not be read, stays the `Err(String)` beside it. Its `Identity` doc
  is also the one place that says which non-edits speak and which stay
  identities on purpose (spec §5.5, §11 #88).
- `edit.rs` — the op enum, `parse` and `apply`. **Its module doc IS the op
  table's SEMANTICS half** — what each op means, and what an absent
  optional argument means — where `op_table.rs` is the ARGUMENTS half;
  `app/Sources/ReelOps.swift`'s typed builders, `AgentCatalog*.swift`'s
  tools and spec §6 mirror the two together. `OP_NAMES` is re-exported from
  here, at the path it has always had. `parse` answers an `Envelope` — the
  op AND the envelope's `scope` — and `apply_op(&Op)` knows nothing about
  nests. The semantics table is the reason this file is over the size cap
  and stays exempt (below).
- `op_table.rs` — the op table as DATA (road map 7's D3): one `OpRow` per
  op and one `Argument` per argument — its name, its `Kind` (`Kind::Output`
  for `set_canvas`'s dynamic range, `Kind::Blending` for its blending),
  whether the
  decoder requires it and, for the few that have one, its `Bound` — and
  `OP_NAMES` as a projection of it, re-exported by
  `edit.rs` so no caller moved. A published interface, where the `Op` enum
  and the dispatch are its implementation. Its one reader in the crate is
  `op_schema.rs`, which carries the rows out through the FFI; the APP's
  reader is every one of the sixty-two op tools in the agent catalog,
  which print these rows instead of restating them. **A `Bound` is
  published only where the core REFUSES outside it** — `set_canvas`'s two
  dimensions, sourced from `edit_canvas.rs`'s own constants, and
  `add_graphic_clip`'s `width` and `height`, from `model_graphic.rs`'s, never
  retyped — and never where it CLAMPS, which is the app's to say in its
  prose. A row holds no prose, no semantics and no default spelled twice;
  `Kind` is closed (nineteen kinds; `Texts`, a list of strings, is
  `set_action_end`'s `off`), carries each vocabulary's members, and has exactly ONE
  kind per answer serde gives, because a distinction the
  decoder cannot see is one no test could prove. Nothing here is the
  authority — the enum's fields are, and `core/tests/op_table.rs` proves
  every row by asking the decoder. Capped at 400 lines like any new module:
  it does NOT inherit `edit.rs`'s table exemption.
- `op_schema.rs` — `op_table.rs` written as JSON Schema, which is what
  `rc_op_schemas` publishes (road map 7's D3·2): one object per op, its
  properties the arguments and its `required` the ones the decoder will not
  do without. **The match over `Kind` is exhaustive** — a kind added to the
  table does not compile until this says what JSON it is — and it is a
  module of its own because a row changes when an OP does and this changes
  when the published DIALECT does. It says nothing about what an argument is
  FOR (the catalog's prose), nothing about what a patch may CARRY
  (`Kind::Object` is an object with no properties; D1 left the core the one
  validator of that), and nothing about `additionalProperties` on an op,
  because the catalog merges `project` and `scope` in afterwards. Tested
  through the FFI in `core/tests/op_schemas.rs`.
- `scope.rs` — editing INSIDE a nest: the envelope's `scope` key. Builds a
  VIEW project from the nest (its tracks and clips at top level, its frozen
  size as the canvas, the parent's rate, media, `next_id` and nests, no
  markers), applies the op to it UNCHANGED, merges back. So `Project::clip`
  keeps its one meaning and no op has a nest-aware branch. Three things are
  counter-intuitive and measured: the scoped nest's own row stays in the view
  with its tracks and clips EMPTIED (removing it dangles every other nest's
  reference; leaving it whole doubles every id under `validate`); the nests
  write-back is union first, orphans after; and **a scoped apply has a wider
  `Err` arm than any unscoped op** — `check_caps` and `check_nesting` are
  document-wide and run on the MERGED parent, so an op valid inside the nest
  can still return `Err`. `refused_inside` is an EXHAUSTIVE match over every
  op, so a new op does not compile until it is classified. The READ half is
  `rc_project_scoped` in `ffi.rs`, which calls the same `scoped_view`.

- `edit_clip.rs` — clip construction and placement callers: `add_clip`, move,

- `edit_clip_timing.rs` — `trim_start`, `trim_end`, `rate_stretch`, `set_speed`,

- `edit_detach.rs` — `detach_audio` and `set_enabled`, a clip's video and

- `edit_commit.rs` — the placement commit protocol: replacements preserve

  straddled one narrowed, presets and motion halves anchored to the two
  ends. Every splitter in the crate routes here, so a rule stated once is a
  rule they all obey. A free function over `&mut Project` because it is
  called mid-edit on a clone the caller is still assembling.

- `patch.rs` — reading a caller-authored patch, cut out of `edit_props.rs`

  refuses `action_past_end` only when the new end is past the clip's end AND
  later than the action's current end (SR-22, #338), so a value-only edit of
  an action a trim left past the end goes through. `nest` and `unnest`
  (fresh ids, content byte-equal; the nest clip on the front-most non-matte
  track, a matte carried only above the copy of its target, unnest aligned on
  the front-most non-matte track — spec §11 MT-5);
  `paste`, whose payload schema is its module doc; `Payload` and
  `parse_payload` are `pub(crate)`, because `edit_paste_attributes.rs` reads
  the same payload.

  the op's `schema` after the three groups' walk (G-34); in an `off` path it
  is an `Err`.

  clip-time → source-time function its speed actions make (the ease
  integrals of `actions.rs`'s curves), `is_ramped` (media clips only),
  `end_speed`'s clamp, `peak_rate` (the greatest rate the clip NAMES, its
  base and every end rate, the ×12 figure, SR-19 (d)), `source_at`, `rate_at`,
  `rate_in_force` (what `clip_state`'s top-level `speed` answers, SR-21); `of_length` (the
  map over any horizon, reading on past the clip's end with its own
  actions, SR-18 (a)), `time_for_source` (its inverse) and `head_end_rate`
  (a split's straddled head re-solved so both halves meet at S(cut),
  SR-18 (e)); what `content_length_in_source` reads for a ramped clip;
  `rate_profile` (the rate over clip time for the lane's rate line: piece
  edges, and `RATE_SAMPLES` + 1 samples across a ramp piece, SR-26).
- `speed_segments.rs` — the map cut into plan pieces: `Held` at one rate
  (an equal-rate action is held), `Ramp` one video segment per canvas
  frame, and the ramp audio map with a breakpoint every 600 ticks;
  `constant_ramp_audio` is the two-point map, flagged `constant`, that
  `evaluate.rs` puts on a constant Keep pitch off time-scaled audio segment
  so Swift renders it as a ramp's (SR-28).

  clip its ramp audio map, byte-equal to the plan segment's `ramp.map`, a
  constant clip its two points, flagged `ramped` as `is_ramped` is; a

  naming the largest end rate that fits (floored to 0.001,
  `largest_fitting_end_rate`, which split's eased tail also uses, over the
  shared `largest_fitting_rate` that `add_speed_ramp` also solves through).
- `edit_action_ramp.rs` — `add_speed_ramp`, the ramp presets (SR-23, #340):
  Ramp Up, Ramp Down, Speed Dip or Speed Burst as ordinary Speed actions in

  missing schema by name (an asset is an ordinary switch, `""` naming no
  image, G-42), and answers each prop's kind and the default for each the
  clip lacks (`schema_default`; an asset's is its string default or `""`); `write_graphic_end` stores `props` and `kinds` by

- `edit_paste_attributes.rs` — `paste_attributes`, cut out of `edit_paste.rs`
  under the size rule as a pure move ahead of spec §11 G-32: the payload's
  EARLIEST clip's property groups (then the front-most, then the lower id —
  never the array's first) copied onto each target, replaced whole and never
  merged. `PasteGroup` is the five names it takes — the four patch groups and
  `graphic`, which is never in the default set: a graphic's `props` copied
  whole onto clips drawn by the SAME module, the target keeping its name,
  size, `in` and `length`, written with `insert` and `shift_remove`
  (`model_graphic.rs`'s rule). A target key the payload lacks that an
  action on the target names (`names_prop`) is kept (G-34 (d), amending
  G-32 (e)). `skip_missing` drops a named group the payload
  clip lacks and skips a target that cannot take one. **The copied props are
  shape-checked once, the first time a target takes them**: a paste nothing
  takes never reads the map. `patch::Group` gains no variant for it.
- `edit_zoom.rs` — `add_zoom_action`, the screencast zoom, and `ZoomRegion`,
  the one op ARGUMENT that is a caller-authored object: its `Deserialize` is
  written out rather than derived so it answers as a patch does — an object
  required (a list is not read member by member), an unknown or missing
  member named, a wrong-typed one named by its path. **Its module doc

  rotation and crop included; it composes `add_action` + `set_action` +

  `add_adjustment_clip`, and the refusals every other door asks it for — a
  transition (from `add_transition`, `set_transition`, `set_transition_style`

  clip on a NEW back-most track, OPS rather than app-side composites because
  the composite carries constraints no half states. A blurred copy drops
  `enabled.audio`, `audio.duck`, the transition, the actions and the label

  match and each pair of entries agrees on its discrete fields (`kind`,

  evaluator's last line of defence (`set_action_end` checks a `video`,
  `audio` or `text` end patch's keys and kinds but deliberately not its
  VALUES, and never looks at the clip for them; this bounds every value
  such a patch can carry and forces `normal` on a nest clip), with
  `bounded` / `finite_or`; the first two a pure move out of `actions.rs`

  as its domain's identity, for `video_json`'s callers),
  `align_identity_curves` (spec §11 GR-12, GR-32: an identity curve
  meeting a curve of another count in an action takes that curve's x's,
  its ends at 0 and 1 on a tone curve and every value the neutral on a
  hue curve, so a grade animates from neutral), and `CurveBlend`,
  `curve_blends` and `blended_curves_json` (spec §11 GR-34: two
  non-identity curves of different counts in an action blend their
  values — the evaluator names each such channel with its clamped end
  curve and the eased t in `Evaluated.curve_blends`, and only the recipe
  layer and `clip_state` write it, as `{from, to, t}`; never a file).
- `actions_qualifier.rs` — `qualifier_json` (spec §11 GR-35): a qualifier
  with its `blur` present even at 0, which `actions.rs`'s `video_json` writes
  for a non-neutral one so the blur animates from 0; and `align_hue_center`
  (spec §11 GR-13): before
  the lerp, an action's target hue centre moves by ±360 when the two
  centres are more than 180° apart, so the centre animates the short
  way round (350 → 10 through 0); `clamp_qualifier` brings it back
  into [0, 360).
- `actions_color.rs` — `blend_colors` (spec §11 G-43): after the spanning
  action's `lerp`, each of the model's colours — `COLOR_POINTERS`' eight
  `[r, g, b, a]` in `video` and `text` and `CHROMA_KEY_POINTER`'s `[r, g,

  action's two ends (`oklab_mix_unit` / `oklab_mix_rgb`), only strictly

  stays exact; an end of the wrong arity keeps §5.4's hold-then-switch.

  version 13, spec §11 G-34): finished actions' `end.graphic.props` laid

  with no start, held and switched at the end. Total. `names_prop` is
